And when you have overtaken them,
‘Why have you returned evil for good?
The cup that you have stolen,
ipse est in quo bibit dominus meus, et in quo augurari solet:
it is that from which my lord drinks, and in which he is accustomed to discern signs.
You have done a very sinful thing.’”
He did as he had been ordered.
et apprehensis per ordinem locutus est.
And having overtaken them, he spoke to them according to the order.
“Why does our lord speak in this way,
ut servi tui tantum flagitii commiserint?
as though your servants had committed such a shameful act?
which we found at the top of our sacks,
reportavimus ad te de terra Chanaan:
we carried back to you from the land of Canaan.
et quomodo consequens est ut furati simus de domo domini tui aurum vel argentum?
So in what way does it follow that we would steal, from the house of your lord, gold or silver?
apud quemcumque fuerit inventum servorum tuorum quod quæris,
Whichever of your servants will be found to have what you seek,
et nos erimus servi domini nostri.
and we shall be the servants of my lord.”
“Let it be according to your verdict.
With whomever it will be found,
Itaque festinato deponentes in terram saccos,
And so, they quickly placed their sacks down to the ground,
incipiens a majore usque ad minimum,
beginning with the oldest, all the way to the youngest,
he found the cup in Benjamin’s sack.
Primusque Judas cum fratribus ingressus est ad Joseph (necdum enim de loco abierat) omnesque ante eum pariter in terram corruerunt.
And Judah, first among his brothers, entered to Joseph (for he had not yet departed from the place) and together they all fell down before him to the ground.
“Why would you choose to act in this way?
an ignoratis quod non sit similis mei in augurandi scientia?
Could you be ignorant that there is no one like me in the knowledge of discerning signs?”
“What could we answer to my lord?
And what would we be able to say,
aut juste poterimus obtendere? Deus invenit iniquitatem servorum tuorum:
or to justly claim? God has discovered the iniquity of your servants.
en omnes servi sumus domini mei,
See, we have all become servants to my lord,
et apud quem inventus est scyphus.
and he with whom the cup was found.”
Absit a me ut sic agam:
“Far be it from me that I should act in this way.
vos autem abite liberi ad patrem vestrum.
But you may go away free to your father.”
loquatur servus tuus verbum in auribus tuis,
my lord, let your servant speak a word in your ears,
and do not be angry with your servant.
For you are next to Pharaoh.
‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
et nos respondimus tibi domino meo:
And we answered you, my lord:
‘There is our father, an old man,
qui in senectute illius natus est:
who was born in his old age.
His brother of the same womb has died,
et ipsum solum habet mater sua,
and he alone is left to his mother and father,
And you said to your servants,
et ponam oculos meos super illum.
and I will set my eyes on him.’
Non potest puer relinquere patrem suum:
‘The boy is not able to leave his father.
For if he sends him away,
And you said to your servants:
Nisi venerit frater vester minimus vobiscum,
‘Unless your youngest brother arrives with you,
you will not see my face any more.’
Cum ergo ascendissemus ad famulum tuum patrem nostrum,
Therefore, when we had gone up to your servant our father,
narravimus ei omnia quæ locutus est dominus meus.
we explained to him all that my lord had spoken.
and buy us a little wheat.’
And we said to him: ‘We cannot go.
si frater noster minimus descenderit nobiscum,
If our youngest brother descends with us,
we do not dare to see the face of the man.’
Vos scitis quod duos genuerit mihi uxor mea.
‘You know that my wife conceived twice by me.
And since then, he has not appeared.
If you take this one also,
et aliquid ei in via contigerit,
and anything happens to him on the way,
deducetis canos meos cum mœrore ad inferos.
you will lead my grey hairs down with grief to the grave.’
Igitur si intravero ad servum tuum patrem nostrum,
Therefore, if I would have gone to your servant, our father,
et puer defuerit (cum anima illius ex hujus anima pendeat),
with the boy not present, (though his life depends upon the life of him)
and if he were to see that he is not with us,
et deducent famuli tui canos ejus cum dolore ad inferos.
and your servants will lead his grey hairs down with sorrow to the grave.
Ego proprie servus tuus sim qui in meam hunc recepi fidem,
Let me be your very own servant, for I accepted this one into my trust,
peccati reus ero in patrem meum omni tempore.
I will be guilty of a sin against my father for all time.’
Manebo itaque servus tuus pro puero in ministerio domini mei, et puer ascendat cum fratribus suis.
And so I, your servant, will remain in place of the boy, in ministry to my lord, and then let the boy go up with his brothers.
Non enim possum redire ad patrem meum, absente puero:
For I cannot return to my father without the boy,
ne calamitatis, quæ oppressura est patrem meum, testis assistam.
lest I appear as a witness to the calamity that will oppress my father.”
